1.title: Pricing Models and Cost Management
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Pricing Models and Cost Management. This module opens the fourth domain of the exam, Billing, Pricing and Support, with task statements four point one and four point two. You will learn how A W S charges, how the E C two purchasing options differ, what data transfer and storage cost, and which tools estimate, track and reduce your bill. This domain is about twelve percent of the exam, so every point counts.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Explain the pricing principles and the E C two purchasing options, and choose among them. Describe data transfer and storage costs. Explain how A W S Organizations consolidates billing and shares discounts. Use the Pricing Calculator, Cost Explorer, A W S Budgets and the Cost and Usage Reports. And explain cost allocation tags and A W S Compute Optimizer.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater Watches Its Bill
1.text: Tidewater is watching its bill. Its steady servers run all year, while nightly image jobs can wait and restart. Photos are served to customers and copied between Regions, and the team wonders what that costs. The shop now has five accounts, and the finance lead wants one bill, and a warning before spending passes a limit. Each project's cost must also be visible. Your job is to choose the pricing options and the cost tools.

1.title: How AWS Pricing Works
1.text: A W S pricing rests on three principles. First, pay as you go: you pay only for what you use, so spending follows your needs. Second, save when you commit: Savings Plans and reservations lower prices in return for a commitment of one or three years. Third, pay less by using more, through tiered pricing. For example, the more you store in Amazon S three, the less you pay per gigabyte. The Free Tier helps new accounts. New accounts receive one hundred U S dollars in credits, with up to one hundred more for completing activities, plus always-free offers. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, a Free account plan lasts up to six months, or until the credits run out. Exam tip: pay as you go, save by committing, and pay less per unit as volume grows.

1.title: EC2 Purchasing: On-Demand, Savings Plans and Reserved Instances
1.text: The exam asks you to choose among the E C two purchasing options. On-Demand means you pay by the second, with no commitment. It fits short-term or unpredictable use. Savings Plans mean you commit to an amount of usage per hour for one or three years. Compute Savings Plans also cover Fargate and Lambda, and apply to any instance family, size, operating system or Region. Reserved Instances are a billing discount for a specific configuration, for one or three years. They come as Standard or Convertible, you can pay all, partial or no upfront, and you cannot cancel them. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, A W S recommends Savings Plans over Reserved Instances, with savings of up to seventy-two percent, or up to sixty-six percent for Compute Savings Plans. Exam tip: a commitment to a dollar amount means Savings Plans; a commitment to a configuration means Reserved Instances.

1.title: EC2 Purchasing: Spot, Dedicated Hosts, Dedicated Instances and Capacity Reservations
1.text: Four more options solve special needs. Spot Instances use spare capacity at a steep discount. E C two can interrupt them with a two-minute notice, and Savings Plans do not cover them, so they suit batch jobs and other interruptible work. Dedicated Hosts are a physical server that is fully yours. They show sockets and cores, let you bring your own per-socket or per-core licenses, and are billed per host. They suit licenses and compliance. Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to one account, are billed per instance, and give no visibility of the host, so they suit isolation without host control. Capacity Reservations reserve capacity in one Availability Zone for any duration, with no discount by themselves. Exam tip: interruptible means Spot; your own licenses mean Dedicated Hosts; guaranteed capacity means Capacity Reservations.

1.title: Choosing a Purchasing Option
1.text: Choose the purchasing option from the need, as the figure shows. Steady, predictable use: Savings Plans, or Reserved Instances for a fixed configuration. Work that can be interrupted: Spot Instances. Short-term or unpredictable use: On-Demand. Your own licenses or strict compliance: Dedicated Hosts, and Dedicated Instances when you only need isolation. A need for capacity in a zone: Capacity Reservations, combined with a discount plan. And in practice you mix them: commitments for the base load, and Spot for the extras. Exam tip: match the need, steady, interruptible, licenses or capacity, to the option.

1.title: Data Transfer Costs
1.text: Moving data can cost money, and the exam tests the pattern. Data into A W S from the internet is free. Data out to the internet is charged, at rates that depend on the Region. Data within the same Availability Zone is free. Data between Availability Zones is typically charged, and so is data between Regions. The figure shows these paths. To reduce transfer costs, keep traffic inside a zone, use CloudFront to serve content, and use gateway endpoints for S three and Dynamo D B, which avoid data transfer charges within a Region. Exam tip: inbound is free; outbound, cross-zone and cross-Region traffic costs money.

1.title: Storage Pricing: Options and Tiers
1.text: Storage pricing follows the tiers you learned in Module eight. With Amazon S three, you pay for what you store, plus requests and data transfer, with no overage charges, and pricing is tiered by volume. S three Standard-I A and One Zone-I A cost less to store, but add a retrieval fee and a thirty-day minimum. The S three Glacier classes have the lowest storage prices, with retrieval fees and minimums of ninety to one hundred eighty days. S three Intelligent-Tiering adds a small monitoring fee per object, with no retrieval fees. Amazon E B S charges for what you provision. Lifecycle rules move data to cheaper tiers automatically. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, the minimums come from the S three user guide. Exam tip: cooler data sits in cheaper tiers, but watch retrieval fees and minimum durations.

1.title: One Bill for Many Accounts: AWS Organizations
1.text: A W S Organizations manages many accounts. The management account pays the charges of all the member accounts. Consolidated billing gives you one bill, and you can still track charges per account. Combined usage shares volume pricing discounts, Reserved Instance discounts and Savings Plans across the accounts, which can lower the total. Consolidated billing has no additional fee. For billing, the organization is treated as one account, so a Reserved Instance bought by one account can discount matching usage in another. If you do not want sharing, you can turn it off in the billing preferences. Exam tip: one bill and shared discounts for many accounts mean consolidated billing in A W S Organizations.

1.title: Estimating Costs: AWS Pricing Calculator
1.text: The A W S Pricing Calculator is a free, web-based planning tool for estimating the cost of A W S services. Use it to model a solution before you build it: pick services, Regions, instance types and payment options. It shows the calculations behind each estimate, grouped by service or by architecture. You can save an estimate as a link, or export it as C S V or P D F. Its prices come from the A W S Price List A P I, and estimates exclude taxes. A version inside the Billing and Cost Management console can use your own discounts and commitments. Exam tip: to estimate before you build, use the A W S Pricing Calculator.

2.title: Tracking Costs: AWS Cost Explorer and AWS Budgets
2.text: Two tools track your spending. A W S Cost Explorer lets you view and analyze costs and usage, with charts, filters and grouping. It keeps thirteen months of history, adds a forecast, and the console is free. Think of it as seeing where the money went. A W S Budgets lets you set cost, usage, and Reserved Instance or Savings Plans budgets. It sends alerts by email or Amazon S N S when actual or forecasted spend crosses a threshold. Think of it as a warning before you overspend. Budgets data updates up to three times a day, so alerts can lag, and budget actions can apply a policy automatically. Exam tip: looking back and forecasting means Cost Explorer; warning on a threshold means A W S Budgets.

2.title: Organizing Costs: Cost Allocation Tags and Cost and Usage Reports
2.text: A cost allocation tag is a label, a key and a value, that organizes your costs by project, owner or application. There are two types: A W S-generated tags, which use the a w s colon prefix, and user-defined tags, which use the user colon prefix. Both must be activated in the Billing and Cost Management console, and tags can take up to twenty-four hours to appear. Activated tags then show up in Cost Explorer and in cost allocation reports. The A W S Cost and Usage Reports hold the most comprehensive cost and usage data. They are delivered to your S three bucket as C S V files, by hour, day or month, with columns for your tags. In an organization, only the management account manages cost allocation tags. Exam tip: tags show cost by project once they are activated, and Cost and Usage Reports hold the detailed data.

2.title: Cutting Costs: Compute Optimizer and the Billing Console
2.text: A W S Compute Optimizer analyzes configuration and utilization metrics, and gives rightsizing recommendations. It also finds idle resources. It covers E C two instances, Auto Scaling groups, E B S volumes, Lambda functions, E C S on Fargate, R D S and more. By default it uses about fourteen days of CloudWatch data, and you must opt in. A W S Billing and Cost Management is the home for the Bills page, payments, credits, Cost Explorer, Budgets, tags and Free Tier tracking. One access rule: I A M users cannot see billing until you activate I A M access, though the root user can by default. Exam tip: rightsizing and finding idle resources mean Compute Optimizer; bills and payments live in the Billing console.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: Pricing and Cost Management
2.text: Here is how the exam frames this module. Commit or not: Savings Plans for a dollar amount, Reserved Instances for a configuration, On-Demand for no commitment. Interruptible, licenses or capacity: Spot, Dedicated Hosts and Capacity Reservations. Data transfer: inbound is free, and outbound to the internet, across zones and across Regions cost money. Storage: cooler tiers cost less to store, but add retrieval fees and minimums. Many accounts: consolidated billing, one bill and shared discounts. Estimate, track and warn: Pricing Calculator, Cost Explorer and Budgets. And organize and save: tags, Cost and Usage Reports, and Compute Optimizer. Exam tip: name the need first.

2.title: Design Check: Tidewater's Cost Plan
2.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Servers that run all year, with room to change families: Compute Savings Plans. Nightly image jobs that can restart: Spot Instances. A server needing its own per-socket licenses: Dedicated Hosts. Cheaper storage for records rarely read: an S three Glacier class, reached with a lifecycle rule. One bill for five accounts, with shared discounts: consolidated billing. A cost estimate before building the new design: the A W S Pricing Calculator. A look back at last quarter's spend: A W S Cost Explorer. An email when forecast spend passes a limit: A W S Budgets. Cost per project in the reports: cost allocation tags. And finding oversized servers: A W S Compute Optimizer. Pause the video if you want more time.

2.title: Try It: A Monthly Cost Budget With an Email Alert (Optional)
2.text: This optional exercise is not tested on the exam, but it shows how alerts work. Use a practice account, and aim to get a warning before spending passes a limit. In the Billing and Cost Management console, open Budgets and choose Create budget. Choose a monthly cost budget with a small amount, and add an alert at eighty percent of actual spend, and another for forecasted spend, sent to your email. Check the Budgets pricing page first: monitoring is free, but budget actions have a daily cost beyond the first two. The command on the screen lists the budgets in an account, and the account I D is only an example. When you finish, delete the budget. Exam tip: hands-on work is not tested on this exam, but it shows how alerts and thresholds work.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. The pricing principles are pay as you go, save when you commit, and pay less by using more. The E C two options are On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, Spot, Dedicated Hosts, Dedicated Instances and Capacity Reservations. For transfer and storage, inbound is free, outbound, cross-zone and cross-Region cost money, and cooler tiers cost less to store. For accounts, consolidated billing gives one bill and shared discounts. And for tools, the Pricing Calculator estimates, Cost Explorer analyzes, Budgets warns, tags and the Cost and Usage Reports organize, and Compute Optimizer rightsizes.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Tidewater's web servers run at a steady level all year, but the team may change instance families and Regions. Which option offers savings for a commitment while keeping that flexibility? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, Compute Savings Plans. They lower prices in exchange for a one- or three-year commitment to a usage amount, and apply regardless of instance family, size, operating system or Region. Spot can be interrupted, Dedicated Hosts target licenses and compliance, and Capacity Reservations give capacity without a discount.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Tidewater's nightly image-resizing jobs can be interrupted and restarted without harm. Which E C two option gives the lowest price for this work? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, Spot Instances. They sell spare E C two capacity at steep discounts, and work that can be interrupted and restarted suits them. Dedicated Instances add isolation at a higher price, On-Demand has no discount, and a three-year commitment is wasted on short jobs.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A company must use its existing per-socket server software licenses on A W S and needs visibility of the sockets and cores. Which option fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, Dedicated Hosts. They give visibility of sockets and cores and support bringing existing per-socket, per-core or per-V M licenses. Dedicated Instances give isolation without that visibility, and Spot and Savings Plans are pricing options that do not control licensing.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Select two. Which two data transfers are free of charge? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and E. Inbound data transfer from the internet, and data transfer within the same Availability Zone, are free. Outbound transfer to the internet, and transfer across Availability Zones or Regions, typically incur charges.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Tidewater wants a cost estimate for a planned architecture before it builds anything. Which tool should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, the A W S Pricing Calculator. It models a solution and estimates its cost before you build it. Cost Explorer and the Cost and Usage Reports describe spending that has already happened, and Budgets warns when spending crosses a threshold.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. The finance lead wants an email when Tidewater's forecast monthly spend is expected to pass a set amount. Which service should Tidewater use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, A W S Budgets. It can alert by email or Amazon S N S when actual or forecasted cost passes a threshold. The Pricing Calculator estimates costs, Artifact provides reports, and Compute Optimizer recommends resource sizes.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. Tidewater now has five A W S accounts in one organization. How are their charges and discounts handled? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. With consolidated billing in A W S Organizations, the management account pays one bill at no extra fee, and usage is combined so volume, Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts are shared. The other options describe behavior that does not exist.

2.title: Practice Question 8
2.text: Question eight. Tidewater applied a user-defined tag named Project to its resources but cannot see it in Cost Explorer. What must it do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Activate the tag as a cost allocation tag in the Billing and Cost Management console. Both A W S-generated and user-defined tags must be activated before they appear in Cost Explorer and cost allocation reports, and then they can take up to twenty-four hours to show.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all eight answers. Question one: B. Question two: D. Question three: A. Question four: A and E. Question five: C. Question six: A. Question seven: D. Question eight: B. That completes Module thirteen. Next, Module fourteen covers A W S Support plans, technical resources and the partner network.
